svg.title: Strategy
svg.desc: Strategy. Put interchangeable algorithms behind one interface and choose one at runtime, instead of branching inside the caller. Step 1, One method, many ifs: shippingCost() branches on the method name: each new rule edits it, and one suite tests every rule. Step 2, Rules become strategies: Each rule becomes a class with cost(order); Checkout holds one and calls strategy.cost(order). Step 3, Swap at runtime: Each click swaps Checkout's strategy: one 3 kg, EUR 42 order costs 4.90, then 4.50, then 15.00. Step 4, Add one without editing: FreeOver50 is one new class: 4.90 for this order, 0.00 for a EUR 57 one. Checkout is untouched.

g.text: shippingCost() branches on the method name: each new rule edits it, and one suite tests every rule.
Each rule becomes a class with cost(order); Checkout holds one and calls strategy.cost(order).
Each click swaps Checkout's strategy: one 3 kg, EUR 42 order costs 4.90, then 4.50, then 15.00.
FreeOver50 is one new class: 4.90 for this order, 0.00 for a EUR 57 one. Checkout is untouched.
a change for one rule re-tests all four
As a function: sort(compareFn), Java's Comparator, Python's key=
vs State: the client picks the strategy; a state picks the next state
vs Template Method: composition, swapped at runtime, not subclassing
In systems: a load balancer's algorithm; a feature flag that picks one
